chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) were twelve thousand: eight thousand from Medina, two thousand from Mecca, and two thousand from the Tulaqa (those who became Muslims after the conquest of Mecca). There were no Qadaris, Murji'is, Kharijites, Mu'tazilites, nor any who acted according to their own opinions. They cried day and night and said, 'Oh Allah! Please take away our souls before we eat barley bread.'

key_terms.الطَّلَقَاءُ: Those who became Muslims after the conquest of Mecca
key_terms.صَاحِبَ رَأْيٍ: One who acts according to their own opinion

ai.seo_question: Who were the twelve thousand companions of the Prophet according to Imam al-Sadiq and what theological sects were absent among them?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the theological purity of the twelve thousand companions by noting the absence of later sects like the Kharijites and Mu'tazilites, affirming their status as the foundational model of orthodoxy in Shia tradition. This narration underscores the concept of 'Ahl al-Bayt's' view that the early community was free from the theological innovations (bid'ah) that emerged after the Prophet's era, linking their intense asceticism to a profound awareness of divine accountability.
